questions.history: Emit two indented objects with distinct foo and bar values as text/event-stream
questions.prediction: The parent is predicted to lose unprefixed continuation lines at the SSE reader. On the merge two dispatched events should each decode to the complete corresponding object in order.
questions.basis: In SSE each physical data line needs its own data field. Blank lines terminate events. Jackson JSON readback establishes whether all fields survived.
questions.refutation: There are fewer or additional events, JSON parsing fails, or any of the four values is missing or crosses the event boundary.

questions.history: Disable indentation, retain the same two beans and SSE writer
questions.prediction: Both revisions should deliver the same two JSON objects in the same order.
questions.basis: Compact JSON needs only one physical data line per event and the existing writer already prefixes the initial line.
questions.refutation: Either event is incomplete or the parser combines the two.

questions.history: On the merge enable indentation again, replace one string value with a string containing an actual LF, and serialize an object nested inside the second event
questions.prediction: The consumer should still dispatch exactly two events. Its parsed fields should retain the embedded LF and the nested property.
questions.basis: An LF inside a JSON string is escaped on the wire, whereas structural pretty-print line breaks each need SSE framing. Varying nesting changes only the latter count.
questions.refutation: An LF within a value creates another event, a continuation is dropped, or the nested object changes.
